claim: On the supplied simultaneous residual event, at every positive time and every registered rule, average actual next-law total variation is at least positive-part residual excess divided by time.
assumptions: An arbitrary measurable observation space, with actual P_s,j and Q_s,j probability measures on that same space.
Each actual test phi_s,j is measurable and pointwise lies in [0,1].
The observed residual is evaluated with the Q-test integral, while drift uses the P-test integral minus the Q-test integral on the same sequence.
The event premise |R_t,j-D_t,j| <= boundary_t,j holds simultaneously at all positive times and registered rules.
The conclusions are pathwise conditional implications. Proposition 66 supplies any probability/confidence interpretation externally.
dependency_graph: lawTV is one half of the total mass of the Hahn-Jordan total variation of the actual signed difference P.toSignedMeasure-Q.toSignedMeasure.
P and Q are finite probability laws, so bounded measurable tests and their centered versions phi-1/2 are integrable.
Signed-measure integral linearity identifies the signed integral of phi-1/2 with integral_P(phi)-integral_Q(phi); equal unit masses cancel the two constant terms.

The centered test has norm <=1/2 everywhere. The vector-measure integral bound with scalar multiplication bilinear map of norm one gives the desired discrepancy bound with constant 1 relative to the probability TV convention.
The absolute drift is bounded by the finite sum of absolute mean discrepancies, hence by the finite sum of actual lawTV values.
The triangle inequality |R| <= |R-D|+|D| and the event premise imply max(|R|-boundary,0) <= |D|.
Transitivity followed by division by positive real t proves the lower certificate.
The simultaneous endpoint specializes this same implication at every t>0 and every j without adding independence or changing the event.

residual_limits: This module does not prove or construct Proposition 66 concentration, its simultaneous event, or its registered false-rejection budget. It proves the exact P68 implication conditional on that event.

Conditional laws at actual histories/actions are supplied as actual probability measures. Existence of regular conditional distributions, their history measurability, predictability, and data-driven estimation are not inferred here.
The rule family is arbitrary for this pathwise implication. A probabilistic simultaneous-event construction for a registered family retains its own countability/budget assumptions.
Failure to cross gives no general TV upper bound, rank certificate, or guarantee for untested actions. The zero-test example demonstrates that limit.
strongest_safe_statement: For arbitrary measurable observation laws and measurable [0,1]-valued tests, the full all-time/all-rule lower-TV certificate holds pathwise on the actual simultaneous residual event. No extra concentration assertion is included.
